name: Coconut rice pudding with mango
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water, then drain it.
Pour the coconut milk and water into a saucepan, add the rice and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Purée the mango until smooth and spoon it over the warm pudding.
Serve warm. Before 9 months, blend everything for a perfectly smooth texture.

name: Apple and date cinnamon sauce
steps: Peel the apples, core them and cut into cubes.
Finely chop the dates.
Put the apples, dates and water in a saucepan, cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the cinnamon and lemon juice, then purée until very smooth.
Serve warm or cold. Before 9 months, pass the sauce through a sieve.

name: Lentil, squash and carrot purée
steps: Cut the butternut squash and the carrot into cubes.
Pour the broth into a saucepan, add the squash and carrot, then simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add the lentils and olive oil, then continue for 5 minutes.
Purée until smooth using the cooking liquid.
Adjust the texture to the child's age: smooth at 6 months, mashed around 9 months.

name: Chicken, sweet potato and green peas
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into cubes.
Pour the broth into a saucepan, add the chicken pieces and the sweet potato, then cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add the peas and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Check that the chicken is cooked through, then add the canola oil.
Purée or mash with a fork, depending on the child's age.

name: Roasted sweet potato sticks
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Peel the sweet potato and cut it into thick sticks, about the width of an adult finger.
Coat with olive oil and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake for 25 minutes, until a stick crushes between two fingers.
Let cool slightly before serving. A stick should give under light pressure.

name: Soft banana oat patties
steps: Mash the banana with a fork.
Mix the rolled oats, banana, applesauce and cinnamon.
Let rest for 5 minutes so the oats absorb the moisture.
Shape into flat patties and brown them in canola oil in a pan, 3 minutes per side.
Let cool slightly. Cut into strips for a child aged 6 to 8 months.

name: Creamy mango oatmeal
steps: Bring the oat beverage to a simmer in a saucepan.
Add the rolled oats and chia seeds, then cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Purée the mango and stir it in off the heat with the cinnamon.
Let cool slightly — the oatmeal thickens as it cools.
Blend before 9 months for a smooth texture.

name: Tender rice flour crêpes
steps: Mix the ground flaxseed with 60 ml of oat beverage and let rest for 5 minutes.
Whisk the rice flour, the remaining oat beverage and the applesauce.
Stir in the flax mixture until the batter is smooth.
Cook in a pan with canola oil, 2 minutes per side.
Serve in finger-width strips.

name: Salmon and Sweet Potato Patties
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F); line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Peel Sweet potato, cut into chunks, and steam 10 minutes until fork-tender.
Mash Sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth; let cool 5 minutes.
Flake cooked Salmon (skin removed) into the bowl with the mashed Sweet potato.
Thinly slice Green onion and chop Fresh dill; add both to the bowl.
Add Egg, Breadcrumbs, and Lemon juice; mix until a firm mixture forms.
Shape mixture into 12 patties about 1.5 cm thick; place on the prepared sheet.
Brush patties lightly with Canola oil on both sides.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, flipping once at 10 minutes, until golden and firm.
Serve with Plain yogurt for dipping. Keeps refrigerated 2 days; freeze up to 1 month.

name: Oat and Banana Energy Bites
steps: Peel and mash 2 Bananas in a large bowl until smooth.
Add Natural peanut butter and Maple syrup to the bowl.
Stir in Cinnamon and Chia seeds until evenly combined.
Add Rolled oats and Raisins; stir to form a thick dough.
Refrigerate the dough for 10 minutes until firm enough to roll.
Roll the dough into 18 balls of about 3 cm each.
Arrange balls on a parchment-lined plate in a single layer.
Serve immediately or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

name: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Patties
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F); line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and cube Sweet potato; microwave 5 minutes until fork-tender.
Mash Sweet potato and Cooked chickpeas together in a large bowl.
Add Egg, Chickpea flour, Ground cumin, Sweet paprika, and Salt.
Mix until a firm dough forms that holds its shape.
Divide into 10 patties about 1.5 cm thick; place on the lined sheet.
Brush each patty lightly with Olive oil on both sides.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and firm.
Cool 5 minutes before serving; store in the fridge up to 3 days.

name: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and cube sweet potato, then steam until fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
Mash sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth and lump-free.
Drain and rinse cooked chickpeas, then add to the bowl.
Mash chickpeas roughly, leaving some texture.
Add egg, chickpea flour, cumin, turmeric, and salt; stir until combined.
Roll mixture into 18 balls and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Brush each bite lightly with olive oil.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool 5 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days.

name: Banana, Oat and Blueberry Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk mashed banana, eggs, plain yogurt, canola oil, maple syrup, and vanilla in a large bowl.
Add oat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, and cinnamon to the bowl.
Stir until just combined; do not overmix.
Fold in blueberries gently with a spatula.
Divide batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature up to 2 days, or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Baked Salmon with Sweet Potato and Broccoli
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and cube Sweet potato into 2 cm pieces; cut Broccoli into small florets.
Mince Garlic and whisk together with Olive oil, Lemon juice, Paprika, and Salt in a small bowl.
Toss Sweet potato cubes with half the olive oil mixture; spread on one side of the baking sheet.
Roast Sweet potato 15 minutes until beginning to soften.
Add Broccoli and Salmon portions to the baking sheet; drizzle remaining olive oil mixture over all.
Roast 12 to 15 minutes until Salmon flakes easily and Sweet potato is golden and tender.
Sprinkle Fresh dill over everything before serving. Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days.

name: Sweet Potato & Oat Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and cube Sweet potato, then steam for 12 minutes until completely tender.
Mash the cooked Sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth.
Add the Egg and Canola oil to the bowl and stir well.
Stir in the Rolled oats and Cinnamon until a thick dough forms.
Scoop tablespoon-sized portions and roll into balls.
Arrange balls on the prepared sheet, spacing 3 cm apart.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Keep refrigerated up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Salmon and Lentil Vegetable Patties
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F); line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Finely grate Zucchini; squeeze firmly in a clean cloth to remove excess water.
Grate cooked Carrot and mince Garlic.
Flake cooked Salmon into a large bowl, removing any bones.
Add Cooked lentils, Egg, grated Zucchini, Carrot, Garlic, Fresh dill, and Lemon juice to the bowl.
Add Oat flour; stir until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Shape into 16 patties about 1.5 cm thick; place on the prepared baking sheet.
Brush patties lightly with Olive oil.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool 5 minutes before serving. Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months.

name: Banana Oat Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mash two ripe bananas in a large bowl until completely smooth.
Add the Unsweetened applesauce, Cinnamon, and Vanilla extract to the bowl.
Stir in the Rolled oats until a thick, cohesive dough forms.
Fold the Blueberries gently into the dough without crushing them.
Scoop tablespoon-sized mounds onto the prepared baking sheet, 2 cm apart.
Flatten each mound slightly with the back of a damp spoon.
Bake 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centres feel set.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a rack.
Makes 18 bites. Store in an airtight container: 3 days at room temperature or 1 month frozen.

name: Chickpea and Sweet Potato Patties
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel the Sweet potato, cube it, and steam until fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
Mash the cooked Sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth.
Drain and rinse the Cooked chickpeas, then add them to the bowl.
Mash the Cooked chickpeas coarsely, leaving some texture in the mixture.
Add the Chickpea flour, Ground cumin, Turmeric, and Lemon juice; stir to combine.
Divide the mixture into 12 equal balls and flatten each into a 1 cm patty.
Place the patties on the sheet and brush the tops lightly with Olive oil.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, flipping once halfway, until firm and golden on both sides.
Makes 12 patties. Store refrigerated for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Salmon and Lentil Patties with Zucchini
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F); line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Combine Ground flaxseed and Water in a small bowl; rest 5 minutes to gel.
Grate Zucchini coarsely, then squeeze firmly in a clean towel to remove excess water.
Flake Salmon into a large bowl, removing any bones.
Add Cooked lentils, Zucchini, Gluten-free breadcrumbs, minced Garlic, Fresh dill, Lemon juice, and Salt.
Add the flaxseed gel and mix until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Shape into 12 patties, each about 1.5 cm thick, and arrange on the prepared baking sheet.
Brush patties lightly with Olive oil on top.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes until golden on top and cooked through.
Cool 5 minutes before serving; refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Baked Salmon with Sweet Potato and Broccoli
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and cut Sweet potato into 2 cm cubes; cut Broccoli into small florets.
Toss Sweet potato and Broccoli with 20 ml Olive oil and Salt on the baking sheet.
Roast vegetables 15 minutes, until Sweet potato begins to soften.
Mince Garlic; whisk with Lemon juice, Dijon mustard, remaining Olive oil, Paprika, and Dill.
Place Salmon portions on the baking sheet alongside the vegetables.
Brush Salmon evenly with the mustard-dill mixture.
Return baking sheet to oven for 12 to 14 minutes, until Salmon flakes easily with a fork.
Check that Sweet potato and Broccoli are golden and tender.
Serve immediately. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container up to 2 days.

name: Lentil and Sweet Potato Patties
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and cube Sweet potato, then steam for 10 minutes until completely tender.
Mash the steamed Sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth.
Mince the Garlic clove finely.
Add Cooked lentils, Egg, Oat flour, Ground cumin, Turmeric, and minced Garlic to the bowl.
Stir the mixture until fully combined and shapeable.
Shape the mixture into 16 patties, each about 1.5 cm thick.
Brush each patty lightly with Olive oil and place on the prepared sheet.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until firm and golden on the outside.
Cool 5 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days, or freeze up to 2 months.

name: Sunflower Banana Oat Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and mash 2 ripe bananas thoroughly in a large bowl.
Add sunflower seed butter and maple syrup to the bowl.
Stir in cinnamon and vanilla extract until combined.
Fold in rolled oats and raisins until a soft dough forms.
Drop tablespoon-sized mounds onto the prepared baking sheet.
Flatten each mound gently with the back of a spoon.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes, until set and lightly golden on the edges.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container up to 3 days, or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Banana & Oat Blender Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Add the Rolled oats to a blender and process for 20 seconds into a coarse flour.
Add the Mashed banana, Eggs, Canola oil, Unsweetened applesauce, and Vanilla extract.
Add the Baking powder and Cinnamon to the blender.
Blend for 30 seconds until smooth and well combined.
Divide the batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups, filling each two-thirds full.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until risen and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Serve at room temperature. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Banana & Chickpea Yogurt Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mash the banana thoroughly in a large bowl until no lumps remain.
Whisk the plain yogurt, canola oil, and vanilla extract into the mashed banana.
Add the chickpea flour, oat flour, baking powder, and cinnamon to the bowl.
Stir gently until just combined; the batter will be thick.
Divide the batter evenly among the 12 cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Serve slightly warm or at room temperature. Store in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze individually for up to 1 month.

name: Cucumber & Ricotta Pita Rounds
steps: Slice each pita bread into 8 wedges using a sharp knife.
Slice the cucumber into thin rounds, about 3 mm thick.
Finely chop the fresh dill.
In a small bowl, stir together the ricotta, lemon juice, olive oil, and dill.
Spread a heaped teaspoon of the ricotta mixture onto each pita wedge.
Place one cucumber round on top of each spread wedge.
Arrange on a plate and serve immediately, or refrigerate up to 4 hours before serving.

name: Turkey and Rice Bowl with Roasted Vegetables
steps: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Dice Zucchini and Red bell pepper into 2 cm cubes.
Toss diced vegetables with 15 ml Olive oil, Salt, and Sweet paprika on the baking sheet.
Roast vegetables 20 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelised at the edges.
Meanwhile, bring Brown rice and Water to a boil in a medium saucepan, then simmer covered 25 minutes, until water is absorbed.
Mince Garlic and sauté in remaining 15 ml Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add Ground turkey and cook 8 to 10 minutes, breaking it apart, until no pink remains.
Stir Ground cumin, Tamari sauce, and Lemon juice into the turkey and cook 1 minute, until combined.
Divide Brown rice among four bowls; top with roasted vegetables and turkey mixture.
Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container up to 3 days.

name: Sweet Potato & Chickpea Mini Patties
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Peel and cube sweet potato into 2 cm pieces.
Steam sweet potato 10 minutes, until completely tender when pierced.
Mash sweet potato and cooked chickpeas together in a large bowl until mostly smooth.
Add egg, chickpea flour, cumin, and turmeric; stir to a firm dough.
Shape the dough into 16 small patties, about 4 cm wide and 1 cm thick.
Place patties on the lined baking sheet and brush tops with olive oil.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool 5 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days.

name: Blueberry Banana Chickpea Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk mashed banana, eggs, plain yogurt, canola oil, and vanilla in a large bowl.
Add chickpea flour and baking powder to the bowl.
Stir gently until just combined; do not overwork the batter.
Fold in blueberries with a spatula, distributing evenly.
Divide batter equally among the 12 muffin cups, filling each three-quarters full.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or refrigerate for 5 days.

name: Blueberry Chickpea Flour Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk together the chickpea flour, baking powder, and cinnamon in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, mash two ripe bananas until smooth.
Add the eggs, canola oil, and vanilla extract to the mashed banana and whisk well.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Fold the blueberries gently into the batter.
Divide the batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze individually for up to 1 month.

name: Mini Cheesy Sweet Potato Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and grease a 24-cup mini muffin tin.
Peel and grate the sweet potato finely into a large bowl.
Grate the cheddar and set it aside.
Add the wheat flour, baking powder, and salt to the bowl with the sweet potato.
In a small bowl, whisk the eggs, cow's milk, and canola oil together.
Pour the egg mixture into the flour bowl and stir until just combined.
Fold in three-quarters of the grated cheddar gently.
Divide the batter evenly among the 24 muffin cups and top with the remaining cheddar.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until golden on top and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin before unmoulding. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Banana Blueberry Oat Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine Rolled oats, Cinnamon, and Baking powder.
Add Mashed banana, Unsweetened applesauce, Maple syrup, Vanilla extract, and Canola oil.
Stir until a thick, uniform dough forms.
Gently fold in Blueberries without crushing them.
Scoop 18 rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared baking sheet.
Flatten each portion lightly with the back of a spoon.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centres are set.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a rack.
Makes 18 bites · 4 family portions. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Mini Patties
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and cube Sweet potato, then microwave for 5 minutes until completely tender.
Mash the cooked Sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth.
Add drained Cooked chickpeas and mash roughly, leaving some texture.
Stir in Chickpea flour, one minced Garlic clove, Ground cumin, Sweet paprika, Salt, and Lemon juice.
Divide the mixture into 12 equal portions and shape each into a flat round patty.
Arrange patties on the prepared baking sheet and brush the tops with Olive oil.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the tops are golden.
Cool for 3 minutes on the sheet before serving.
Makes 12 patties · 4 family portions. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Mini Sweet Potato and Oat Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and grease a 12-cup mini muffin tin.
Peel and grate the sweet potato; measure out 150 g of packed grated flesh.
In a large bowl, whisk together oat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, and cinnamon.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, maple syrup, canola oil, cow's milk, and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients; stir until just combined.
Fold in the grated sweet potato evenly throughout the batter.
Spoon the batter into the muffin tin, filling each cup to the top.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Chickpea and Cucumber Yogurt Dip with Pita
steps: Drain and rinse the cooked chickpeas thoroughly in a colander.
Peel and mince the garlic clove finely.
Halve and deseed the cucumber, then dice into small 0.5 cm cubes.
Add chickpeas, plain Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, and cumin to a food processor.
Blend for about 60 seconds until the dip is smooth and creamy.
Transfer the dip to a medium bowl and stir in the diced cucumber and fresh dill.
Cut each pita bread into 6 small triangles suitable for toddler hands.
Serve the dip in the bowl alongside the pita triangles for dipping.
Store leftover dip covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days; keep pita separate.

name: Banana & Chickpea Energy Balls
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then pat them dry with a clean cloth.
Mash the chickpeas and mashed banana together in a large bowl until mostly smooth.
Add the sunflower seed butter and maple syrup; stir to combine.
Stir in the rolled oats and cinnamon until a firm dough forms.
Refrigerate the dough for 10 minutes so it is easier to shape.
Scoop the dough into 16 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Arrange the balls on a plate in a single layer.
Serve immediately or refrigerate. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Sweet Potato & Oat Patties
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and cube the sweet potato into 3 cm pieces.
Steam the sweet potato for 12 minutes, until completely tender, then mash smooth.
Stir ground flaxseed into water in a small bowl; rest 5 minutes until gel forms.
Combine mashed sweet potato, rolled oats, chickpea flour, cinnamon, and flaxseed gel in a large bowl.
Shape the mixture into 16 round patties, about 1.5 cm thick each.
Brush each patty lightly with olive oil on both sides.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, flipping once halfway, until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving. Store refrigerated up to 3 days, or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Banana & Chickpea Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Drain and rinse the cooked chickpeas, then mash them thoroughly with a fork until mostly smooth.
Add mashed banana, canola oil, vanilla extract, and cinnamon to the chickpeas; stir well.
Fold in oat flour and baking powder until a soft, uniform dough forms.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared sheet, spacing 3 cm apart.
Gently flatten each mound to about 2 cm thick with the back of a spoon.
Bake 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are set and the tops feel dry to the touch.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container up to 3 days, or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Banana & Oat Blender Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and lightly grease a 24-cup mini-muffin tin with canola oil.
Combine mashed banana, unsweetened applesauce, sunflower seed butter, and vanilla extract in a large bowl.
Add rolled oats, cinnamon, and baking powder to the bowl.
Stir until a thick, uniform batter forms with no dry patches.
Spoon the batter evenly into all 24 cups of the mini-muffin tin.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes, until the tops are set and lightly golden.
Let cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.
Serve once fully cooled to a safe temperature. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or refrigerate for up to 5 days.

name: Lentil and Sweet Potato Bowl
steps: Peel and dice Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely chop Onion and mince Garlic.
Cook Rice according to package directions; set aside and keep warm.
Heat Olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat until shimmering.
Add Onion and Garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Stir in Ground cumin and Turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Sweet potato, Crushed tomatoes, and Unsalted vegetable broth; stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until sweet potato is fork-tender.
Stir in Cooked lentils and Spinach; cook for 2 minutes until spinach wilts.
Serve the lentil mixture over Rice. Keeps refrigerated up to 3 days; freeze portions up to 1 month.

name: Turkey and Zucchini Rice Skillet
steps: Cook Brown rice according to package directions; set aside.
Dice Zucchini and Bell pepper into small cubes; finely chop Onion and mince Garlic.
Heat Olive oil in a large 30 cm skillet over medium-high heat.
Add Onion and Garlic; cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until translucent.
Add Ground turkey; cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in Dried oregano and Sweet paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Zucchini, Bell pepper, Crushed tomatoes, and Unsalted chicken broth; stir to combine.
Simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes, until vegetables are tender and sauce thickens.
Serve over Brown rice. Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Lentil and Sweet Potato Rice Bowl
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 1 cm cubes.
Combine rice and water in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and cook for 18 minutes until water is absorbed.
Warm olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sweet potato cubes and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Stir in cooked lentils, cumin, and turmeric, mixing to coat evenly.
Pour in vegetable broth and simmer for 5 minutes until the mixture is saucy and fragrant.
Spoon lentil mixture over rice in bowls. Mash portions for babies under 9 months. Keeps refrigerated for 3 days.

name: Ground Turkey and Zucchini Quinoa Skillet
steps: Rinse quinoa under cold water, then combine with water in a saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook for 15 minutes until quinoa is fluffy and water is absorbed.
Trim and dice zucchini into 1 cm pieces; slice cooked carrot into thin rounds.
Mince the garlic clove finely.
Warm olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, then add ground turkey.
Cook turkey for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add garlic, zucchini, carrot, oregano and crushed tomatoes to the skillet.
Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are soft.
Serve turkey mixture over quinoa. Mash or blend for babies under 9 months. Keeps refrigerated for 3 days.

name: Banana and Chickpea Soft Cookies
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Drain and rinse the cooked chickpeas, then mash them in a large bowl until mostly smooth.
Add the mashed banana and unsweetened applesauce to the bowl and stir to combine.
Mix in the vanilla extract and cinnamon until evenly distributed.
Add the oat flour and baking powder, then stir until a soft dough forms.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the baking sheet, pressing each into a flat round.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the cookies are set and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Chicken and Zucchini Rice Bowl
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
Dice the chicken into small 1 cm pieces; slice the zucchini into thin half-moons.
Mince the garlic clove finely.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat; add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken pieces and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until no pink remains.
Stir in the rice, sliced cooked carrot, zucchini, turmeric, and unsalted chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and mash or chop the chicken to an age-appropriate texture before serving.
Yield: 4 family portions. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 days, or freeze in portions for up to 1 month.

name: Chicken and Sweet Potato Rice Bowl
steps: Cook Rice in 600 ml water in a covered saucepan over medium heat for 18 minutes, until all water is absorbed.
Peel and dice Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; dice cooked Carrot to the same size.
Mince 2 cloves of Garlic finely.
Cut Chicken into small 1 cm pieces, removing any tendons.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add Garlic and Sweet potato; cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until sweet potato is fork-tender.
Add Chicken pieces and Turmeric; cook for 6 to 7 minutes, until no pink remains.
Pour in Unsalted chicken broth and cooked Carrot; simmer for 3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Spoon mixture over Rice; serve warm. Yields 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days.

name: Turkey and Sweet Potato Rice Bowl
steps: Peel and dice Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely dice Onion and mince Garlic.
Cook Rice according to package directions in a medium saucepan; set aside.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, 180 °C (350 °F).
Add Onion and Garlic; cook 3 to 4 minutes, until softened and translucent.
Add Ground turkey; cook 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it apart, until no pink remains.
Stir in Sweet potato, Cumin, Turmeric, and Salt; stir well to coat.
Pour in Unsalted chicken broth; cover and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until Sweet potato is fork-tender.
Spoon Rice into bowls and top with the turkey and sweet potato mixture.
Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days.

name: Salmon and Lentil Spinach Bowl
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place Salmon skin-side down on the sheet; drizzle with 10 ml Olive oil and season with Salt.
Bake Salmon 12 to 14 minutes, until it flakes easily with a fork.
Meanwhile, rinse Quinoa and cook in 400 ml Water in a medium saucepan, 12 to 15 minutes, until fluffy.
Finely dice Onion and mince Garlic; cook in remaining Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, 3 minutes.
Add Cooked lentils to the skillet; stir and heat through for 2 minutes.
Add Spinach; cook 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until wilted.
Stir in Lemon juice and Fresh dill; remove from heat.
Flake baked Salmon into large pieces and serve over Quinoa with the lentil and spinach mixture.
Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days.

name: Lentil, Zucchini and Tomato Pasta
steps: Dice the onion finely; mince the 2 garlic cloves; slice the zucchini into thin half-moons.
Cook the rice pasta in a large pot of boiling water for 8 minutes, until tender; drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add the minced garlic and the tomato paste; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the zucchini, the crushed tomatoes, and the dried basil; stir to combine.
Simmer over low-medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is tender.
Stir in the cooked lentils and heat for 2 minutes until warmed through.
Toss the sauce with the rice pasta. Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days.

name: Ground Turkey and Vegetable Rice Bowl
steps: Rinse Rice under cold water, then combine with 600 ml Water in a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low; cover and cook 18 minutes until absorbed.
Peel and finely dice Onion; mince 2 cloves Garlic; dice Zucchini into 1 cm cubes.
Slice Carrot (cooked) into thin half-moons, about 3 mm thick.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add Onion and Garlic; cook 3 minutes, stirring, until softened and fragrant.
Add Ground turkey; cook 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up with a spoon, until no pink remains.
Add Zucchini, Carrot (cooked), Ground ginger and Tamari sauce; stir and cook 4 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Spoon Rice into bowls and top with the turkey and vegetable mixture.
Serve immediately; refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Banana & Avocado Rice Cakes
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and lightly brush a 12-cup mini muffin tin with canola oil.
Combine the mashed banana and mashed avocado in a large bowl and stir until smooth.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir to incorporate evenly into the banana mixture.
Add the rice flour and baking powder, stirring gently until just combined with no dry streaks.
Spoon the batter into the prepared tin, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes, until the tops spring back lightly when touched.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.
Serve at room temperature. Store in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Ground Beef and Sweet Potato Coconut Bowl
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet or saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes, until softened.
Add the lean ground beef and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it apart, until fully browned.
Stir in the turmeric and ground ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste, coconut milk, and unsalted vegetable broth; stir well to combine.
Add the sweet potato cubes, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, until the sweet potato is fork-tender.
Stir in the spinach and cook uncovered for 2 minutes, until wilted.
For babies under 9 months, mash the sweet potato pieces lightly before serving.
Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze in portions for up to 2 months.

name: Raspberry Oat Soft Bars
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 23 x 13 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine rolled oats, oat flour, cinnamon, and baking powder.
Add mashed banana, unsweetened applesauce, melted coconut oil, and maple syrup to the bowl.
Stir until a thick, uniform dough forms, with no dry patches remaining.
Gently fold raspberries into the dough, keeping them as whole as possible.
Press the dough evenly into the prepared pan, smoothing the top with a spatula.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until the top is lightly golden and the centre is set.
Cool completely in the pan, then slice into 12 bars.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Eggplant and Lentil Tomato Skillet
steps: Dice the eggplant into 1 cm cubes; peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the eggplant cubes; cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and tender.
Stir in the cumin, paprika and salt; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth; stir well to combine.
Add the cooked lentils; simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the lemon juice; remove from heat.
Serve warm over rice or with soft bread. Keeps refrigerated for 3 days or frozen for 1 month.

name: Apple Cinnamon Oat Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and grate the apple finely, then squeeze out excess moisture with your hands.
In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats, cinnamon, and baking powder.
Add the unsweetened applesauce, mashed banana, and canola oil to the bowl.
Fold in the grated apple until a soft, scoopable dough forms.
Scoop heaped tablespoons of dough onto the lined baking sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart.
Flatten each mound gently with the back of a spoon to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centres feel set.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Green Pea and Chicken Rice Bowl
steps: Cook Rice according to package directions; set aside and keep warm.
Peel and finely dice Onion, mince Garlic, and slice Carrot (cooked) into small rounds.
Cut Chicken into small bite-sized cubes, no larger than 1 cm.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, about 180 °C (350 °F).
Add Onion and Garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add Chicken and Turmeric; cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until no pink remains.
Add Carrot (cooked), Green peas and Unsalted chicken broth; simmer 4 to 5 minutes, until peas are tender.
Stir in Lemon juice and remove from heat.
Spoon the pea and chicken mixture over Rice in shallow bowls.
Serve 4 family portions immediately; refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days.

name: Green Pea and Lentil Coconut Soup
steps: Peel and dice Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely dice Onion; mince Garlic and Ginger.
Heat Coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat, about 180 °C (350 °F).
Add Onion, Garlic and Ginger; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Stir in Cumin and Turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Sweet potato, Cooked lentils, Unsalted vegetable broth and Coconut milk; stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until sweet potato is very tender.
Add Green peas; simmer for 3 more minutes until peas are bright and soft.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup to a creamy but slightly chunky texture.
Stir in Lemon juice; ladle into bowls for 4 family portions.
Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Zucchini and Lentil Tomato Skillet
steps: Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic; cut the zucchini into small 1 cm cubes.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened and translucent.
Add the zucchini cubes and cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the cumin and turmeric; cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the cooked lentils, crushed tomatoes, and unsalted vegetable broth; stir to combine.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, until the zucchini is very tender.
Stir in the nutritional yeast and remove from heat.
Serve warm, mashed lightly with a fork for younger babies. Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Plum and Chia Yogurt Cups
steps: Halve and pit 4 Plums, then slice each half into thin wedges.
Place the Plum slices in a small saucepan with Lemon juice, Maple syrup, and Cinnamon.
Cook over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the Plums are soft and jammy.
Remove from heat and mash the cooked Plums lightly with a fork; let cool for 5 minutes.
In a medium bowl, stir Plain yogurt, Chia seeds, and Vanilla extract together until combined.
Let the yogurt mixture rest for 5 minutes so the Chia seeds begin to thicken it.
Divide the Plain yogurt mixture among 4 small cups and spoon the warm Plum compote on top.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate for up to 2 days with the compote stored separately.

name: Zucchini and Chickpea Tomato Skillet
steps: Cook rice according to package directions; keep warm until serving.
Peel and finely dice onion; mince garlic; trim and dice zucchini into 1 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened and fragrant.
Add diced zucchini; cook for 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until just tender.
Stir in drained cooked chickpeas, crushed tomatoes, cumin, paprika, and vegetable broth.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Serve the skillet over warm rice in shallow bowls.
Makes 4 family portions; store leftovers refrigerated for up to 3 days or freeze for 1 month.

name: Zucchini and Lentil Coconut Soup
steps: Peel and dice onion; mince garlic and fresh ginger; trim and chop zucchini into rough chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Stir in turmeric and cumin; cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add zucchini, drained cooked lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer; cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until zucchini is very tender.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup, leaving some texture.
Stir in lemon juice and ladle into bowls.
Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.

name: Pear and Oat Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel, core and finely grate 2 Pears into a large bowl; press lightly to remove excess juice.
Add Rolled oats, Mashed banana and Cinnamon to the bowl with the grated Pear.
Stir the mixture until a soft, uniform dough forms; do not overmix.
Lightly grease your hands with Canola oil and roll the dough into 18 small balls, about 3 cm each.
Arrange the balls on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart; press each one gently to flatten slightly.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are set and the tops feel firm to the touch.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving; store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

name: Pear and Chia Compote Cups
steps: Peel, core and dice 3 Pears into small cubes, about 1 cm each.
Place the diced Pear in a small saucepan with Water over medium heat.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the Pear is very soft and beginning to break down.
Remove from heat; stir in Cinnamon and Vanilla extract.
Mash the cooked Pear gently with a fork to reach a smooth but slightly textured consistency.
Stir in Chia seeds until evenly distributed throughout the warm compote.
Divide the compote into 4 small cups or ramekins; let stand for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Serve warm or at room temperature; refrigerate leftovers in sealed jars for up to 3 days.

name: Salmon and Coconut Rice Bowl
steps: Combine Rice, Coconut milk, Water, and Turmeric in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 18 minutes until rice is tender.
Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place Salmon skin-side down on the sheet; drizzle with Olive oil and Lemon juice.
Bake Salmon for 12 to 15 minutes, until flesh flakes easily and no pink remains at the centre.
Meanwhile, mince Garlic and sauté in a small pan with a little Olive oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced Carrot (cooked) and Spinach; stir over medium heat for 3 minutes until wilted.
Flake cooked Salmon into large chunks, discarding the skin and any bones.
Divide coconut rice into bowls; top with vegetables, Salmon, and Fresh dill.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days.

name: Salmon and Lentil Coconut Soup
steps: Peel and dice Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; peel and slice Carrot (cooked); dice Onion; mince Garlic.
Heat Olive oil in a large pot over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add Onion and Garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Stir in Turmeric and Ground ginger; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add Sweet potato, Carrot (cooked), Cooked lentils, Coconut milk, and Unsalted vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until sweet potato is very tender.
Nestle Salmon pieces into the simmering soup; cook for 6 to 8 minutes until salmon flakes easily.
Remove Salmon, flake into chunks discarding any bones, then return to the pot.
Stir in Lemon juice and ladle into bowls; blend partially for younger babies if needed.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Peach and Chia Yogurt Cups
steps: Peel and roughly chop 3 peaches, then place them in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add lemon juice and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the peaches are very soft and jammy.
Remove from heat and mash the cooked peach with a fork into a smooth compote.
Stir chia seeds into the warm peach compote and let the mixture rest for 5 minutes to thicken.
In a medium bowl, stir vanilla into plain yogurt until combined.
Spoon the yogurt into 4 small cups or jars, filling each about halfway.
Top each cup with an even layer of peach chia compote.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate for up to 2 days; stir before serving if the layers have settled.

name: White Bean and Sweet Potato Coconut Soup
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes; peel and dice the onion.
Mince the garlic cloves and grate the fresh ginger.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and cook for 4 minutes, until softened.
Add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and turmeric; stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato cubes, drained cooked white beans, unsalted vegetable broth, and coconut milk.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sweet potato is very tender.
Use an immersion blender to blend the soup until smooth and creamy.
Stir in the lemon juice and adjust consistency with a splash of water if needed.
Serve warm in bowls. Refrigerate up to 3 days, or freeze in portions up to 2 months.

name: Carrot and Chickpea Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Drain and rinse the Cooked chickpeas, then pat them dry with a clean towel.
Mash the Cooked chickpeas in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth, some texture remaining.
Stir in the Carrot (cooked), mashed or finely grated, the Egg, Chickpea flour, Ground cumin, and Turmeric.
Mix until a firm, scoopable dough forms with no dry flour visible at the bottom.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough and roll into 18 balls; place on the prepared baking sheet.
Press each ball gently to flatten into a disc about 1.5 cm thick.
Brush the tops lightly with Olive oil using a pastry brush or your fingers.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Carrot Coconut Chia Cups
steps: Purée the Carrot (cooked) with 60 ml of the Coconut milk in a blender until completely smooth.
Pour the remaining Coconut milk into a large bowl or jug.
Whisk in the Chia seeds, Maple syrup, Cinnamon, and Vanilla extract until well combined.
Stir in the carrot purée until the mixture is evenly orange and smooth.
Divide the mixture among 4 small glasses or jars, about 150 ml each.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until fully set and pudding-like.
Stir each cup gently before serving to loosen any settled chia seeds.
Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; do not freeze.

name: Ground Beef and Vegetable Pasta Skillet
steps: Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic cloves; dice the zucchini into 1 cm cubes.
Cook the rice pasta in a large pot of boiling water for 8 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add the lean ground beef; cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomato paste, dried oregano, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Add the zucchini, crushed tomatoes, and unsalted vegetable broth; stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered for 8 minutes, until the zucchini is tender and the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the drained rice pasta to the skillet; stir gently and cook 1 minute to warm through.
Serve warm. Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Ground Beef Stuffed Bell Peppers
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and lightly grease a 23 x 33 cm baking dish with olive oil.
Cook the rice in 360 ml of water in a small saucepan for 15 minutes, until water is absorbed; set aside.
Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic cloves.
Slice the tops off the bell peppers and remove seeds and membranes; set the peppers upright in the baking dish.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; add the onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Add the lean ground beef; cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomato paste, ground cumin, sweet paprika, and salt; cook 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and cooked rice; stir to combine and remove from heat.
Spoon the beef and rice filling evenly into the four bell peppers, pressing gently.
Bake uncovered for 25 minutes, until the peppers are tender. Serves 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days.

name: Apple and Oat Soft Bars
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 20 x 20 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
Peel, core, and finely grate the 2 apples into a large bowl.
Add the unsweetened applesauce and canola oil to the grated apple and stir to combine.
Add the rolled oats, oat flour, cinnamon, and baking powder to the bowl.
Stir until a thick, uniform batter forms with no dry pockets remaining.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared pan, pressing it down gently with a spatula.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until the top is golden and the centre feels firm to the touch.
Cool completely in the pan, then cut into 16 bars.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Apple and Coconut Chia Cups
steps: Peel, core, and roughly chop the 2 apples into small chunks.
Place the apple pieces, lemon juice, and cinnamon in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apple is very soft and saucy.
Remove from heat and mash the cooked apple with a fork to a smooth, thick compote.
Whisk together the coconut milk, chia seeds, and vanilla extract in a medium bowl.
Divide the coconut chia mixture evenly among 4 small cups or jars.
Spoon the warm apple compote over the chia layer in each cup.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until the chia layer is fully set and pudding-like.
Store covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days; stir before serving if needed.

name: Green Pea and Chicken Pasta Skillet
steps: Dice the onion finely and mince the garlic cloves.
Cut the chicken into small 1 cm cubes, suitable for toddlers.
Cook the rice pasta in a large pot of boiling water for 8 minutes, until tender; drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft.
Add the chicken cubes; cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until no pink remains.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth; stir in the dried basil and salt.
Add the green peas; simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until the peas are tender and the sauce thickens.
Fold in the drained rice pasta; stir gently for 1 minute over low heat to combine.
Serve warm. Makes 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Zucchini and Chicken Quinoa Skillet
steps: Rinse quinoa under cold water and set aside.
Peel and finely dice the onion and mince the garlic cloves.
Trim the zucchini and grate them coarsely; set aside.
Cut chicken into small 1 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook for 3 minutes, until softened and fragrant.
Add chicken cubes; cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Stir in quinoa, grated zucchini, cumin, turmeric and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat; cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until quinoa is fluffy and liquid is absorbed.
Serve in bowls; refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Zucchini and White Bean Tomato Skillet
steps: Cook rice in water in a small saucepan over medium heat for 18 minutes, until tender; set aside.
Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic cloves.
Trim the zucchini and slice into thin half-moons about 5 mm thick.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook for 3 minutes, until translucent.
Add zucchini slices; cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until slightly softened.
Stir in drained white beans, crushed tomatoes, dried basil and oregano.
Simmer uncovered for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Serve over rice, mashing beans and zucchini slightly for younger babies.
Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Plum and Oat Soft Bars
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 20 x 20 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
Halve and pit 3 plums, then chop the flesh into small pieces roughly 1 cm.
In a large bowl, combine rolled oats, oat flour, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Add mashed banana, melted coconut oil, and vanilla extract to the dry mixture.
Stir until a soft, cohesive dough forms, then fold in the chopped plum pieces.
Press the mixture evenly into the prepared pan to about 1.5 cm thickness.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until the top is golden and the edges are set.
Cool completely in the pan, then cut into 16 bars.
Serve at room temperature. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Plum and Coconut Yogurt Swirl Cups
steps: Halve and pit 4 plums, then chop the flesh into rough 2 cm pieces.
Place chopped plum, water, cinnamon, and maple syrup in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the plum is completely soft and saucy.
Remove from heat and stir in chia seeds; let the mixture sit for 5 minutes to thicken.
Mash the plum mixture with a fork until it reaches a smooth, jammy consistency.
Divide coconut yogurt evenly among 4 small cups or bowls.
Spoon the plum compote over the yogurt and swirl gently with a spoon.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate covered for up to 24 hours before serving.

name: Pear and Ricotta Rice Cakes
steps: Peel and grate 2 Pears; squeeze out excess juice with your hands.
In a large bowl, whisk 2 Eggs with Ricotta and Vanilla extract until smooth.
Add Rice flour, Baking powder, and Cinnamon; stir until a thick batter forms.
Fold in the grated Pear until evenly distributed.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat, 180 °C (350 °F), and brush with Canola oil.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the skillet; flatten gently with the back of a spoon.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and set through with no wet centre.
Transfer to a wire rack; repeat with remaining batter. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat in a dry pan if desired.

name: Pear and Coconut Chia Pudding Cups
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk Coconut milk, Chia seeds, Vanilla extract, and Cinnamon together.
Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight, until thick and set.
Peel, core, and dice 2 Pears into small cubes; toss with Lemon juice and Maple syrup.
Cook the diced Pear in a small saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until just softened.
Remove the Pear from heat and let it cool to room temperature.
Spoon the chia pudding evenly into 4 small cups.
Top each cup with the cooked Pear pieces and serve.
Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; add the Pear topping just before serving.

name: White Bean and Spinach Rice Skillet
steps: Peel and finely dice the Onion; mince the Garlic cloves.
Rinse the Cooked white beans under cold water and drain well.
Heat Olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat.
Add Onion and Garlic; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened and translucent.
Stir in Ground cumin and Sweet paprika; cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add Rice, Crushed tomatoes and Unsalted vegetable broth; stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in Cooked white beans and Spinach; cook uncovered for 2 minutes, until spinach wilts.
Remove from heat and mash a few beans with the back of a spoon for a creamier texture suitable for babies.
Serve warm. Yields about 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: White Bean and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry
steps: Peel and dice the Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; peel and finely dice the Onion; mince Garlic and fresh Ginger.
Cook Brown rice according to package directions in a medium saucepan; set aside and keep warm.
Heat Coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add Onion, Garlic and Ginger; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Stir in Turmeric and Ground cumin; cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add Sweet potato cubes, Crushed tomatoes and Coconut milk; stir to combine.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until sweet potato is fork-tender.
Stir in drained Cooked white beans; cook uncovered for 3 minutes, until heated through.
Mash a few beans and sweet potato pieces for a smoother texture suitable for babies.
Spoon curry over Brown rice to serve. Yields 4 family portions. Refrigerate for up to 3 days.

name: Carrot and Oat Mini Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and lightly grease a 24-cup mini muffin tin with canola oil.
Steam cooked carrot until very tender, about 8 minutes, then mash with a fork until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk together oat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, and cinnamon.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, mashed banana, canola oil, and cow's milk until combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir gently until just incorporated.
Fold in the mashed carrot until evenly distributed throughout the batter.
Divide the batter among the 24 mini muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Keep refrigerated up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Carrot and Ricotta Rice Cakes
steps: Steam cooked carrot until very tender, about 8 minutes, then mash until smooth with a fork.
Mince the garlic clove finely and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the mashed carrot, ricotta, parmesan, and minced garlic.
Add the egg, rice flour, and fresh dill; stir until a soft, cohesive batter forms.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, about 170 °C (340 °F).
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the skillet and flatten gently into 7 cm rounds.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and set through with no raw centre.
Transfer to a plate lined with paper towel. Keep refrigerated up to 2 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Cod and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato into 2 cm cubes; finely dice the onion; mince the garlic and ginger.
Start the rice in a medium saucepan according to package directions; keep warm.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and crushed tomatoes; add the sweet potato and stir to combine.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 12 minutes, until the sweet potato is just tender.
Cut the white fish (cod, haddock) into 4 cm chunks; nestle into the sauce.
Cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir in the lemon juice; serve over rice — about 20 portions · 4 family portions; keeps refrigerated up to 2 days.

name: Banana Coconut Chia Pudding Cups
steps: Peel and slice 2 bananas into thin rounds; set aside half for topping.
Mash the remaining banana slices in a large bowl until smooth.
Add coconut milk, vanilla, maple syrup, and cinnamon to the mashed banana.
Whisk until evenly combined and no lumps remain.
Stir in chia seeds and mix well to distribute them throughout the mixture.
Pour into 4 individual cups or jars, dividing evenly.
Top each cup with the reserved banana slices.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until fully set and pudding-like.
Serve cold. Keeps covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Turkey and Spinach Coconut Curry
steps: Peel and dice sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely dice onion; mince garlic.
Cook rice according to package directions in a medium saucepan; set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, about 180 °C (350 °F).
Add onion and garlic; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add ground turkey; cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking apart, until no pink remains.
Stir in turmeric, cumin, and ground ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sweet potato cubes and coconut milk; simmer over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until sweet potato is fork-tender.
Stir in spinach; cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Serve over rice. Yields approximately 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days.

name: Sweet Potato and Coconut Bliss Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and dice the sweet potato, then steam for 10 minutes until completely tender.
Mash the steamed sweet potato in a large bowl until fully smooth with no lumps.
Add the rolled oats, ground flaxseed, cinnamon, and vanilla extract to the bowl.
Pour in the coconut milk and melted coconut oil, then stir until a thick dough forms.
Roll the dough into 18 balls of about 2 cm each and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Gently flatten each ball into a small disc about 1 cm thick using your palm.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until firm to the touch and lightly golden on the edges.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Sweet Potato and Lentil Coconut Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and cube the sweet potato, then boil for 10 minutes until soft and drain well.
Mash the sweet potato and cooked lentils together in a large bowl until mostly smooth.
Mince the garlic clove and add it to the bowl with the turmeric and ground cumin.
Add the rice flour and coconut milk, then mix until a firm, scoopable mixture forms.
Drizzle the olive oil over the baking sheet and spread it lightly with a brush.
Scoop 16 portions of the mixture onto the sheet and flatten each to about 1.5 cm thick.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, flipping once halfway, until golden and firm on both sides.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Date & Oat Energy Balls
steps: Soak pitted dates in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain well.
Place soaked pitted dates in a food processor and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Add rolled oats, sunflower seed butter, cinnamon, and vanilla extract to the processor.
Pulse until the mixture comes together into a firm, slightly sticky dough.
If the dough is too dry, add water one teaspoon at a time and pulse again.
Scoop out tablespoon-sized portions and roll firmly between your palms into balls.
Place the 16 balls on a plate and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes to firm up.
Serve chilled; store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days.

name: Date, Banana & Coconut Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Soak pitted dates in warm water for 5 minutes, drain, then finely chop them.
In a large bowl, combine mashed banana, coconut milk, and melted coconut oil.
Add oat flour, baking powder, and cinnamon to the bowl and stir until just combined.
Fold the chopped pitted dates evenly through the batter.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the bites are set and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving; store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

name: Quinoa, Lentil and Sweet Potato Skillet
steps: Peel and dice Sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; peel and finely dice Onion; mince Garlic.
Rinse 180 g of Quinoa under cold water in a fine-mesh sieve.
Combine Quinoa and 360 ml of Water in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; cook Onion and Garlic for 3 minutes until softened.
Add Sweet potato cubes; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until edges begin to soften.
Stir in Ground cumin, Turmeric, and Sweet paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Cooked lentils, Crushed tomatoes, and Coconut milk; stir to combine.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until Sweet potato is tender when pierced.
Spoon Quinoa into bowls and top with the lentil and Sweet potato mixture.
Serve warm. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Melon and Chia Coconut Cups
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together coconut milk, chia seeds, maple syrup, and the juice of 1 lime.
Refrigerate the chia mixture for at least 10 minutes, stirring once halfway, until thickened.
Meanwhile, peel and deseed the melon, then cut it into small 1 cm cubes.
Divide the thickened chia pudding evenly among 4 small cups or bowls.
Spoon 1 tablespoon of coconut yogurt over each cup.
Top each cup with an even portion of the diced melon.
Serve immediately, or cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours. Makes 4 family portions.

name: Melon and Oat Soft Bars
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 20 x 20 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
Peel and deseed the melon, then grate it finely and squeeze out excess liquid with a clean cloth.
In a large bowl, combine rolled oats, oat flour, cinnamon, and baking powder.
Add mashed banana, canola oil, and egg to the dry ingredients and stir until a thick dough forms.
Fold in the grated melon until evenly distributed throughout the dough.
Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the prepared pan, smoothing the top with a spatula.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until the top is golden and the centre feels set when pressed.
Cool completely in the pan, then cut into 12 bars. Makes 4 family portions; keep refrigerated up to 3 days.

name: Black Bean and Sweet Potato Coconut Bowl
steps: Cook 300 g rice in 600 ml water over medium heat for 18 minutes, until tender and water is absorbed.
Peel and dice sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; peel and finely dice onion; mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add garlic, cumin, and turmeric; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sweet potato cubes and unsalted vegetable broth; cover and cook for 10 minutes until sweet potato is fork-tender.
Stir in drained cooked black beans and coconut milk; simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Squeeze lime juice over the pan and stir gently to combine.
Spoon rice into bowls and ladle the black bean and sweet potato mixture on top.
Serve warm; store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Black Bean and Zucchini Tomato Skillet
steps: Rinse quinoa; combine with 500 ml water in a saucepan and bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 15 minutes until absorbed.
Dice onion and bell pepper; slice zucchini into half-moons; mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and bell pepper; cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add garlic, cumin, and paprika; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced zucchini and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until slightly tender.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and drained cooked black beans; stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until sauce thickens and zucchini is fully soft.
Spoon quinoa into bowls and top with the black bean and zucchini skillet mixture.
Serve warm; refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Beet & Oat Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and finely grate the beet into a large bowl, yielding about 120 g.
Add the mashed banana and canola oil to the bowl with the grated beet.
Stir in the rolled oats, oat flour, baking powder, and cinnamon until a soft dough forms.
Scoop tablespoon-sized portions and roll them into 18 balls; place on the prepared sheet.
Flatten each ball gently with the back of a spoon to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are set and the tops feel firm to the touch.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Beet & Chickpea Coconut Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and coarsely grate the beet; squeeze out excess moisture using a clean cloth.
Mash the drained cooked chickpeas in a large bowl until mostly smooth with some texture.
Add the grated beet, chickpea flour, ground flaxseed, cumin, coconut milk, and coconut oil to the bowl.
Mix until a firm dough forms; if it feels wet, add a little more chickpea flour.
Divide into 16 equal portions and roll each into a ball; place on the prepared sheet.
Flatten each ball slightly and bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until firm and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving. Store refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Tofu and Vegetable Rice Skillet
steps: Cook brown rice in 600 ml unsalted vegetable broth in a covered saucepan over low heat for 25 minutes.
Drain firm tofu and press for 10 minutes; crumble into rough pea-sized pieces with your hands.
Dice zucchini into 1 cm pieces; grate carrot (cooked); mince garlic; roughly chop spinach.
Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add crumbled tofu and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden on most sides.
Push tofu to one side; add remaining 10 ml olive oil, garlic, zucchini, and carrot to the skillet.
Cook vegetables for 4 minutes over medium heat, stirring, until tender.
Stir in spinach and tamari; cook for 1 minute until spinach wilts.
Add cooked brown rice to the skillet and toss everything together over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle with ground sesame seeds; yields about 4 family portions — refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months.

name: Blueberry Chia Coconut Yogurt Cups
steps: Place 150 g of blueberries in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the blueberries for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until they burst and release their juice.
Remove from heat and mash the cooked blueberries lightly with a fork.
Stir in 20 g of chia seeds and 60 ml of coconut milk into the warm blueberry mixture.
Add 2 ml of vanilla extract and stir to combine; let the mixture rest for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Divide 240 ml of coconut yogurt evenly among 4 small jars or cups.
Spoon the blueberry chia mixture over the coconut yogurt in each cup.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate; keeps for up to 2 days in sealed jars.

name: Blueberry Oat Coconut Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine 160 g of rolled oats, 2 g of cinnamon, and 4 g of baking powder.
Add 120 g of mashed banana, 60 ml of coconut milk, and 30 ml of coconut oil to the bowl.
Stir until a soft, uniform dough forms with no dry patches remaining.
Gently fold in 120 g of blueberries, taking care not to crush them.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the bites are golden on the edges and set in the centre.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving; keeps for up to 3 days in an airtight container or freeze for 1 month.

name: Cod and Zucchini Rice Skillet
steps: Dice the onion finely and mince the garlic cloves.
Trim the zucchini and cut into small 1 cm cubes.
Cut the white fish (cod) into 3 cm chunks, removing any bones.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add the rice and zucchini; stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in the unsalted chicken broth and bring to a simmer; cover and cook 15 minutes.
Lay the cod chunks over the rice; cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes, until fish flakes easily.
Drizzle with lemon juice and scatter fresh dill over the top.
Flake the cod into smaller pieces before serving. Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate up to 2 days.

name: Cod, Sweet Potato and Spinach Bowl
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Dice the onion finely and mince the garlic cloves.
Cut the white fish (cod) into 3 cm chunks, removing any bones.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, until softened.
Add sweet potato cubes and turmeric; stir and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the unsalted vegetable broth; cover and cook 10 minutes, until sweet potato is tender.
Nestle the cod chunks into the pan; cover and cook 5 to 6 minutes, until fish flakes easily.
Stir in the spinach and lemon juice; cook 1 minute until wilted.
Break cod into smaller pieces before serving. Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate up to 2 days.

name: Banana & Coconut Oat Flatbread
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and mash 2 ripe bananas with a fork until completely smooth in a large bowl.
Add coconut milk and coconut oil to the mashed banana and stir to combine.
Stir in oat flour, cinnamon, and baking powder until a soft, spreadable batter forms.
Spread the batter evenly onto the parchment paper into a rectangle about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centre feels set to the touch.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then cut into 16 small finger-sized pieces.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate for up to 4 days.

name: Banana & Sunflower Quinoa Bites
steps: Rinse quinoa under cold water, then cook it in 400 ml water for 12 minutes until absorbed.
Spread cooked quinoa on a plate and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and mash 1 large ripe banana until smooth in a large bowl.
Add sunflower seed butter, ground flaxseed, vanilla, and cinnamon to the bowl and stir well.
Fold in the cooled quinoa until a firm, scoopable mixture forms.
Roll heaped tablespoons of mixture into 18 balls and place them on the prepared sheet.
Flatten each ball gently with the back of a spoon to about 1.5 cm thick.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes, until the bites are golden and firm on the outside.
Cool completely before serving; refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

name: Turkey Breast and Butternut Squash Coconut Skillet
steps: Cook Rice in water in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 18 minutes, until tender and water is absorbed.
Peel and dice Butternut squash into 1.5 cm cubes; dice Onion; mince Garlic; slice Turkey breast into thin strips.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Add Onion and Garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened and golden.
Add Turkey breast strips; cook for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until no pink remains.
Stir in Turmeric and Ground cumin; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Butternut squash and Coconut milk; simmer uncovered for 12 to 14 minutes, until squash is fork-tender.
Stir in Spinach and cook for 2 minutes, until wilted.
Serve the skillet over cooked Rice; divide into 4 bowls. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days.

name: Ground Turkey and Lentil Stuffed Bell Peppers
steps: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F); line a large baking dish with parchment paper.
Slice the tops off Bell peppers and remove seeds; place peppers upright in the baking dish.
Dice Onion finely and mince Garlic.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; add Onion and Garlic and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add Ground turkey; cook for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until fully browned with no pink.
Stir in Cooked lentils, Crushed tomatoes, Ground cumin, and Sweet paprika; simmer for 4 minutes until thickened.
Spoon the filling evenly into the 4 Bell peppers; top each with Mozzarella.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until peppers are tender and cheese is melted and golden.
Serve one stuffed pepper per adult portion, halved for toddlers. Refrigerate for up to 2 days.

name: Sweet Potato Coconut Flatbread Triangles
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and cube sweet potato, then steam for 12 minutes until completely tender.
Mash the cooked sweet potato in a large bowl until smooth with no lumps.
Add coconut milk and olive oil to the mashed sweet potato and stir to combine.
Stir in rice flour, cinnamon, and baking powder until a soft, pliable dough forms.
Divide dough into 2 balls; press each into a thin round, about 5 mm thick, on the prepared sheet.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are golden and the surface feels dry.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then cut each round into 8 triangles.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Sweet Potato and Sunflower Pinwheel Bites
steps: Peel and cube sweet potato, then steam for 12 minutes until very tender.
Mash the cooked sweet potato in a medium bowl until completely smooth.
Stir sunflower seed butter, cinnamon, maple syrup, and ground flaxseed into the mashed sweet potato.
Lay both flour tortillas flat on a clean work surface.
Spread the sweet potato mixture evenly over each tortilla, reaching close to the edges.
Roll each tortilla tightly into a firm log and press the edge to seal.
Refrigerate the rolls for 10 minutes so they hold their shape when cut.
Slice each roll into 8 rounds, about 2 cm thick, using a sharp knife.
Arrange pinwheels on a plate and serve; refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days.

name: Cauliflower and Chickpea Tomato Skillet
steps: Cook rice in water in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 18 minutes, until water is absorbed; set aside.
Cut cauliflower into small florets; peel and dice the onion; mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Stir in cumin, paprika, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Add cauliflower florets and crushed tomatoes; stir to combine.
Cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until cauliflower is fork-tender.
Stir in cooked chickpeas and cook uncovered for 3 more minutes, until heated through.
