Serve over rice, mashing or cutting florets further for young babies. Yields 4 family portions. Refrigerate for up to 3 days.

name: Date and Coconut Bliss Bites
steps: Soak pitted dates in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain well.
Place drained dates in a food processor and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Add sunflower seed butter, coconut milk, vanilla extract, and cinnamon to the processor.
Blend again until the mixture is fully combined and pulls away from the sides.
Transfer mixture to a large bowl and stir in rolled oats and chia seeds.
Roll heaped tablespoons of mixture into 16 firm balls between your palms.
Arrange bites on a parchment-lined plate and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes until firm.
Serve 4 bites per portion. Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

name: Date and Mango Chia Pudding Cups
steps: Soak pitted dates in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Peel and dice mango into small pieces, reserving half for topping.
Blend soaked dates, half the mango, coconut milk, vanilla extract, and lemon juice until smooth.
Pour blended mixture into a large bowl and whisk in chia seeds thoroughly.
Let mixture rest for 5 minutes, whisk once more to prevent clumping.
Divide mixture evenly among 4 small cups or jars.
Refrigerate cups for at least 2 hours, or overnight, until fully set.
Top each cup with the reserved diced mango before serving. Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days.

name: Quinoa and White Bean Tomato Skillet
steps: Rinse 200 g of quinoa under cold water; set aside.
Dice 1 onion and 200 g of zucchini into small pieces; mince 2 garlic cloves.
Heat 15 ml of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook for 3 minutes, until softened and translucent.
Add zucchini, 2 g of oregano, and 1 g of dried basil; cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in 400 g of crushed tomatoes and 240 g of cooked white beans, drained and rinsed.
Add rinsed quinoa and 400 ml of unsalted vegetable broth; stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 15 minutes, until quinoa is tender and liquid absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve warm directly from the skillet.
Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Melon & Coconut Chia Freezer Bites
steps: Peel and seed the melon, then cut the flesh into rough chunks.
Place the melon chunks in a blender and blend until completely smooth.
Pour the melon purée into a medium bowl.
Add the coconut milk, chia seeds, and vanilla extract to the bowl.
Stir well and let the mixture rest for 10 minutes so the chia seeds swell.
Stir once more, then spoon the mixture into a 16-cup silicone mini-mould.
Freeze for at least 3 hours, until the bites are fully solid.
Pop the bites out of the mould and serve straight from the freezer. Store frozen for up to 4 weeks.

name: Tofu and Broccoli Quinoa Stir-Fry
steps: Rinse the quinoa; bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan, add quinoa, cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Drain and press the firm tofu for 10 minutes, then cut into 2 cm cubes.
Cut the broccoli into small florets; slice the red bell pepper and cooked carrot into thin strips; mince garlic and fresh ginger.
Whisk together the tamari, cornstarch, and 30 ml water in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat 15 ml canola oil in a large non-stick skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add the firm tofu cubes and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on most sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining canola oil to the skillet; stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the broccoli, red bell pepper, and carrot; stir-fry for 4 minutes until just tender.
Return the tofu to the skillet, pour over the sauce, and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is coated and glossy.
Serve over quinoa and sprinkle with ground sesame seeds. Keeps refrigerated for 3 days or frozen for 1 month.

name: Blueberry & Chia Coconut Freezer Bites
steps: Line a 24-cup mini silicone mould or a flat tray with parchment paper.
Place blueberries in a small saucepan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until they burst and release their juice.
Remove from heat and mash the blueberries lightly with a fork into a rough purée.
Stir in coconut yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup, and vanilla extract until fully combined.
Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes so the chia seeds begin to thicken it.
Spoon the mixture evenly into the prepared mould, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Freeze for at least 2 hours, until firm and set all the way through.
Pop bites out of the mould and serve straight from frozen. Store in an airtight container in the freezer for up to 4 weeks.

name: Blueberry & Banana Oat Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
In a large bowl, whisk together mashed banana, eggs, canola oil, maple syrup, and vanilla extract.
Add oat flour, baking powder, and cinnamon to the bowl and stir until just combined.
Fold in blueberries gently so they stay mostly whole.
Divide the batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Let muffins cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Banana Coconut Quinoa Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cook the quinoa in water according to package instructions, then spread flat to cool for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the mashed banana and coconut milk until smooth.
Stir the chia seeds and cinnamon into the banana mixture and let stand for 3 minutes.
Add the cooled quinoa to the bowl and fold gently until evenly combined.
Brush the parchment lightly with coconut oil, then drop tablespoonfuls of mixture onto the sheet.
Flatten each mound slightly with the back of a spoon to form small rounds.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until firm to the touch and golden at the edges.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Banana and Mango Chia Cups
steps: Peel the banana and cut into chunks; peel and dice the mango into small pieces.
Place the banana chunks and coconut milk in a blender and blend until completely smooth.
Pour the banana mixture into a medium bowl and stir in the chia seeds, cinnamon, and vanilla extract.
Let the mixture rest for 8 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until slightly thickened.
Divide the mango pieces evenly among 4 small serving cups.
Spoon the banana chia mixture over the mango in each cup.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Stir before serving if made ahead.

name: Sweet Potato Coconut Chia Cups
steps: Peel the sweet potato, cut into chunks, and steam for 12 minutes until very tender.
Transfer the steamed sweet potato to a blender with the coconut milk.
Add the cinnamon, vanilla extract, and maple syrup to the blender.
Blend on high for 30 seconds until perfectly smooth and creamy.
Pour the mixture into a large bowl and whisk in the chia seeds evenly.
Divide the mixture among 6 small cups or jars, roughly 70 ml each.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight, until the chia seeds have set the pudding firm.
Serve cold directly from the cups. Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; do not freeze.

name: Cauliflower and Lentil Tomato Skillet
steps: Cut Cauliflower into small florets; dice Onion finely; mince Garlic.
Heat Olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add Onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add Garlic, Sweet paprika, and Dried oregano; stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add Cauliflower florets and Tomato paste; stir well to coat everything.
Pour in Crushed tomatoes and Unsalted vegetable broth; stir to combine.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until Cauliflower is tender.
Stir in drained Cooked lentils and Spinach; cook uncovered for 3 minutes until Spinach wilts.
Sprinkle with Parmesan. Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months.

name: Date, Carrot and Coconut Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and finely grate the cooked carrot; squeeze out any excess moisture with a clean cloth.
Finely chop the pitted dates, then mash them with a fork until a rough paste forms.
In a large bowl, mix the oat flour, ground flaxseed, cinnamon, and ground ginger together.
Add the date paste, grated carrot, coconut milk, and coconut oil to the bowl; stir until a firm dough forms.
Roll the dough into 18 balls of about 2 cm and place them on the prepared baking sheet.
Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand to form small rounds.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until firm to the touch and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Quinoa, Chicken and Spinach Coconut Bowl
steps: Rinse 200 g of quinoa under cold water using a fine-mesh sieve.
Combine quinoa and 400 ml of water in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes until water is absorbed.
Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Cut 300 g of chicken into small, even pieces, about 1 cm thick.
Heat 15 ml of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; cook onion and garlic for 3 minutes until softened.
Add chicken pieces, cumin and turmeric; cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains.
Pour in 200 ml of coconut milk and add 80 g of spinach; stir and cook for 2 minutes until spinach wilts.
Spoon cooked quinoa into bowls and ladle the chicken and coconut mixture over the top.
Serve warm; store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Melon and Coconut Yogurt Swirl Cups
steps: Peel and deseed 400 g of melon, then cut the flesh into small chunks.
Blend the melon chunks until completely smooth using a blender or immersion blender.
Squeeze half a lime over the melon purée and stir to combine.
In a medium bowl, stir the coconut yogurt with the vanilla extract until smooth.
Add the chia seeds to the coconut yogurt and stir well to distribute evenly.
Let the yogurt mixture sit for 5 minutes so the chia seeds begin to swell.
Spoon half the yogurt mixture into 4 small cups or jars.
Divide the melon purée evenly over the yogurt layer in each cup.
Top with the remaining yogurt mixture and swirl gently with a spoon.
Serve immediately or refrigerate; keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Melon and Quinoa Chia Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and deseed 300 g of melon, then purée the flesh using a blender until smooth.
Combine the chia seeds with the coconut milk in a small bowl; let stand 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix the cooked quinoa, melon purée, and chia seed mixture together.
Add the cinnamon and coconut oil to the bowl and stir until fully combined.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart.
Flatten each portion gently with the back of a spoon to form small round bites.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are set and lightly golden.
Cool on the baking sheet for 10 minutes before serving; the bites firm up as they cool.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Salmon, Spinach and Quinoa Skillet
steps: Rinse the quinoa under cold water and set aside. Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add the rinsed quinoa, crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, paprika, and salt; stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 14 to 16 minutes until the quinoa is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Nestle the salmon pieces, skin removed and cut into 4 cm chunks, into the skillet over the quinoa.
Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir in the spinach and lemon juice; cook uncovered for 1 to 2 minutes until the spinach has wilted.
Serve directly from the skillet. Makes 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days; do not freeze.

name: Peach and Coconut Oat Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and pit the peaches, then dice them finely into small soft pieces.
In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats, cinnamon, and diced peach.
Add the mashed banana, coconut milk, and coconut oil to the bowl.
Stir until the mixture holds together and no dry oats remain.
Scoop tablespoon-sized rounds onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until set and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: White Bean and Vegetable Coconut Skillet
steps: Rinse 180 g quinoa under cold water and cook according to package directions; set aside.
Dice the onion, slice 2 zucchini into half-moons, and dice 2 cooked carrots.
Mince 2 garlic cloves.
Melt coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute.
Cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, stirring, until translucent.
Add zucchini and cooked carrot; cook for 4 minutes, until slightly softened.
Stir in cooked white beans, turmeric, and ground ginger; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and unsalted vegetable broth; simmer for 8 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Spoon the white bean and vegetable mixture over the cooked quinoa in bowls.
Serve warm; mash or blend portions for younger babies. Makes 4 bowls · 4 family portions. Refrigerate for up to 3 days.

name: Ground Beef and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry
steps: Peel and dice sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely dice onion; mince garlic and ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add garlic and ginger; stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add lean ground beef and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it apart, until no pink remains.
Stir in turmeric and cumin, coating the beef evenly.
Add diced sweet potato and coconut milk; stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until sweet potato is fork-tender.
Stir in spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted.
Serve warm over rice or mashed; keeps refrigerated for 2 days or frozen for 1 month — 4 family portions.

name: Apple and Lentil Coconut Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel, core, and finely grate the apple; squeeze out as much juice as possible.
Mash the cooked lentils in a large bowl until mostly smooth with some texture remaining.
Add the grated apple, egg, coconut milk, cinnamon, and ground ginger to the lentils; stir to combine.
Stir in the oat flour until the mixture holds together and can be shaped.
Roll the mixture into 18 small balls using about 1 tablespoon each; place on the prepared sheet.
Brush each bite lightly with coconut oil, then flatten slightly with the back of a spoon.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until set and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool completely before serving. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Chickpea and Spinach Tomato Skillet
steps: Peel and finely dice the onion; mince the garlic cloves.
Cook the rice in a saucepan with the water over medium heat for 18 minutes, until tender and water is absorbed.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, paprika, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and add the cooked chickpeas; stir to combine.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the spinach and the salt; stir for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts completely.
Serve the chickpea and spinach mixture over the cooked rice. Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Raspberry Chia Coconut Cups
steps: Place 200 g of raspberries in a small saucepan over low heat.
Cook the raspberries for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until they break down into a loose compote.
Remove from heat and mash any remaining pieces with the back of a fork.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the coconut milk, chia seeds, and vanilla extract.
Stir the raspberry compote into the coconut milk mixture until evenly combined.
Divide the mixture evenly among 4 small cups or jars.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until the chia seeds have fully set and the mixture is thick.
Top each cup with the remaining 50 g of fresh raspberries and a spoonful of coconut yogurt before serving.
Serve chilled. Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Raspberry Oat Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats, ground flaxseed, cinnamon, and baking powder.
Add the mashed banana and melted coconut oil to the dry ingredients and stir to form a soft dough.
Gently fold in the raspberries, being careful not to crush them completely.
Scoop the dough into 20 small rounds using a tablespoon and place them on the prepared baking sheet.
Flatten each round slightly with the back of a wet spoon to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until the bites are set and lightly golden on the bottom.
Allow the bites to cool on the sheet for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
Serve at room temperature. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Eggplant and Chickpea Coconut Curry
steps: Cook the rice according to package directions; set aside and keep warm.
Dice the eggplant into 2 cm cubes; finely dice the onion, mince the garlic, and grate the ginger.
Heat the coconut oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and ginger; cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the turmeric and cumin; cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the eggplant cubes; stir to coat and cook for 5 minutes, until slightly golden.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and coconut milk; stir well to combine.
Add the cooked chickpeas; simmer over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until eggplant is very tender.
Mash a few chickpeas and eggplant pieces into the sauce for a smoother texture for young babies.
Serve over the cooked rice. Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.

name: Green Pea and Sweet Potato Coconut Mash Bowl
steps: Peel and dice sweet potato into 2 cm cubes; mince garlic.
Warm olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add garlic and cumin; stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sweet potato cubes and water; cover and cook for 12 minutes until fork-tender.
Add green peas and coconut milk; cook uncovered for 4 minutes until peas are bright and soft.
Remove from heat and add lemon juice; mash with a fork to a chunky purée.
Divide into bowls and let cool to a safe temperature before serving.
Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Green Pea and Salmon Rice Bowl
steps: Rinse rice; cook in 400 ml water in a medium saucepan for 18 minutes until absorbed.
Mince garlic and grate fresh ginger; flake salmon into 2 cm pieces, removing any bones.
Warm olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add garlic and ginger; stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add salmon pieces; cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until no pink remains.
Add green peas, coconut milk, and coconut aminos; stir and cook for 3 minutes until peas are tender.
Spoon cooked rice into bowls and top with the salmon and pea mixture.
Makes 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Cucumber and Greek Yogurt Dip Cups
steps: Wash and peel one Cucumber, then grate it coarsely over a clean kitchen towel.
Squeeze the towel firmly to remove as much liquid as possible from the grated Cucumber.
Peel and finely mince the Garlic clove.
In a medium bowl, combine Plain Greek yogurt, grated Cucumber, minced Garlic, and Lemon juice.
Add chopped Fresh dill and Olive oil; stir gently until evenly mixed.
Slice the second Cucumber into thick rounds, about 1 cm each, to use as scoops.
Divide the yogurt dip into 4 small cups and arrange Cucumber rounds alongside.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate covered for up to 2 days.

name: Cucumber and Avocado Rice Bites
steps: Cook Rice according to package instructions, then spread on a tray and cool for 10 minutes.
Peel and pit the Avocado, then mash it in a small bowl with Lemon juice until smooth.
Peel the Cucumber and dice it finely into 5 mm cubes.
In a large bowl, combine cooled Rice, mashed Avocado, diced Cucumber, Chia seeds, and Tamari sauce.
Stir gently until the mixture holds together; add a few drops of water if too dry.
Using wet hands, shape the mixture into 20 small oval bites, about 30 g each.
Sprinkle ground Sesame seeds lightly over each bite.
Arrange on a lined plate and refrigerate for 10 minutes to firm up before serving.
Serve chilled; keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Makes 20 bites · 4 family portions.

name: Zucchini and Ground Turkey Tomato Bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and lightly oil a 23 x 33 cm baking dish.
Peel and dice the onion finely; mince the garlic cloves.
Trim and slice the zucchini into rounds about 5 mm thick.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, until softened.
Add the ground turkey and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, and salt; simmer for 3 minutes.
Spoon half the turkey sauce into the baking dish; layer the zucchini rounds on top, then cover with the remaining sauce.
Sprinkle nutritional yeast evenly over the surface.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until the zucchini is tender and the top is lightly golden.
Serves 4 family portions; refrigerate leftovers in a sealed container for up to 3 days.

name: Plum and Quinoa Chia Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cook quinoa in 300 ml of water over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until water is absorbed.
Pit and finely dice 3 plums; transfer to a small saucepan over low heat.
Cook the plums for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened into a rough compote.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, oat flour, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Add the coconut oil and the plum compote; stir until a cohesive dough forms.
Scoop tablespoon-sized portions onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing 3 cm apart.
Flatten each portion gently with the back of a spoon to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until firm to the touch and lightly golden on the edges.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Plum and Avocado Rice Smash Cups
steps: Cook brown rice in 400 ml of water in a medium saucepan for 18 to 20 minutes, until tender.
Pit and peel 4 plums; slice them thinly and set aside.
Cook the plum slices in a small non-stick pan over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until very soft.
Halve and pit 2 avocados; scoop the flesh into a medium bowl.
Add the lemon juice and ground ginger to the avocado; mash with a fork until smooth.
Fluff the cooked brown rice and divide it evenly among 4 small cups or bowls.
Spoon the mashed avocado over the rice in each cup, then top with the soft plum slices.
Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 1 day; do not freeze.

name: Salmon and Lentil Tomato Bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F); lightly oil a 23 x 33 cm baking dish with a little olive oil.
Dice the onion finely; mince the garlic; slice the zucchini into half-moons about 5 mm thick.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; cook the onion for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika, and oregano; stir for 30 seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes and cooked lentils.
Simmer the lentil-tomato mixture for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, then fold in the zucchini.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly.
Lay the salmon fillets on top; drizzle with lemon juice and scatter the fresh dill over the fish.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Flake the salmon into large pieces before serving. Yields 4 family portions; refrigerate for up to 2 days.

name: Peach and Avocado Chia Smash Cups
steps: Peel and pit Peach, then cut into rough chunks and place in a medium bowl.
Halve and pit Avocado, scoop the flesh into the same bowl.
Add Lemon juice and smash everything together with a fork until chunky but spreadable.
Stir in Chia seeds and Vanilla extract until evenly distributed.
Spoon Plain yogurt into the base of each of 4 small cups, about 15 ml per cup.
Top each cup with an equal portion of the peach-avocado smash.
Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes so the Chia seeds thicken the mixture slightly before serving.
Serve chilled. Store covered in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours; do not freeze.

name: White Bean and Ground Turkey Tomato Bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F); lightly grease a 23 x 33 cm baking dish with olive oil.
Peel and dice 1 onion; mince 2 garlic cloves; dice 1 red bell pepper into small pieces.
Heat 30 ml of olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the diced onion and red bell pepper; cook for 4 minutes, until slightly softened.
Add 300 g of ground turkey and the minced garlic; cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains.
Stir in 30 g of tomato paste, 400 g of crushed tomatoes, 2 g of oregano, and 2 g of cumin.
Add 400 g of cooked white beans; stir well and season with 1 g of salt.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish; bake for 15 minutes, until bubbling at the edges.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving over rice or with bread.
Yield: 4 family portions. Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.

name: Carrot and Coconut Milk Soft Bites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and finely grate 200 g of Carrot (cooked) into a large bowl.
Add 15 g of Ground flaxseed and 80 ml of Coconut milk; stir and rest for 5 minutes.
Add 120 g of Oat flour, 4 g of Baking powder, and 2 g of Cinnamon to the bowl.
Pour in 30 ml of Coconut oil and stir until a soft, uniform dough forms.
Scoop tablespoon-sized rounds onto the prepared sheet, spacing them 3 cm apart.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the bites are set and lightly golden on the bottom.
Cool completely on the sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Ground Beef and Lentil Tomato Bowl
steps: Cook brown rice according to package directions; set aside and keep warm.
Peel and finely dice the onion and the cooked carrot; mince the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, about 180 °C (350 °F).
Add the diced onion and minced garlic; cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add lean ground beef; cook for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it apart, until no pink remains.
Stir in ground cumin and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cooked lentils, diced cooked carrot, crushed tomatoes, and unsalted vegetable broth.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens.
Spoon brown rice into bowls and top with the beef and lentil tomato mixture.
Serve warm; refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Chickpea and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato into 1 cm cubes; finely dice the onion; mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, and turmeric; stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato, chickpeas, crushed tomatoes, coconut milk, and water; stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, until the sweet potato is completely tender.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 2 minutes, until wilted.
Mash a few chickpeas and sweet potato pieces against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce slightly.
Serve warm over rice or with soft flatbread. Makes 4 family portions. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
